issues.body: `_assert_dockerfile_provisions_selftest_deps` removes only lines whose first non-space character is `#`, then uses `grep -qF` for the probe substring. A Dockerfile such as `RUN true # jq --version` and `RUN true # python3 -c 'import yaml'` passes both checks even though the shell treats the probe text as comments and executes neither probe. Inert quoted text such as `RUN printf '%s' "jq --version"` is also accepted. This contradicts the function's load-bearing claim that every dependency is proven by a build-time command and leaves the check fail-open. The added comment fixture does not detect this because it tests only whole-line comments.
issues.fix_hint: Validate that each required probe is an actually executed shell command in a RUN instruction, rather than searching for its bytes. At minimum, parse RUN shell continuations and reject probe occurrences in shell comments/quotes or command arguments; preferably structure the Dockerfile stanza in a machine-checkable form that permits exact command-token/command-position validation. Add reject fixtures for inline shell comments and quoted/echoed probe strings, and confirm those rows fail while the real executed probes pass.
issues.title: Text containment accepts probes that never execute

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The image change itself installs and executes the two current dependency probes, and the gate is wired fail-closed for the model Dockerfile. However, the new assertion does not establish its stated security property: it accepts probe text anywhere on a non-full-line-comment Dockerfile line, including shell comments and inert quoted strings. The tests cover only full-line Dockerfile comments, so the marquee proof-vs-install claim remains vacuous against a realistic inert-probe mutation.
